title: Single-forward-pass rule-application task
description: A task where the model is shown a small set of in-context rules mapping inputs to a single-token label, then one input, and must answer immediately with one token. Designed to measure latent (non-CoT) computation, scaled by rule count, hop depth, and precedence interactions rather than by tokenization quirks.

family.description: Task family. Procedural families have generators; semantic ones are hand-written.

prompt.description: Fully rendered prompt as sent to the model. Ends by demanding a single-token answer.

rules.description: Rules in display order. Kept structured so the prompt can be re-templated.

answer.description: Gold answer. Must be a member of answer_space and a single token in mainstream tokenizers (A-Z, 0-9, or a very common short word).

answer_space.description: All labels the model could legitimately produce. Chance accuracy is 1/len.

difficulty.description: Knobs that were used to make the item harder. Absent knobs mean 'not applicable'.

hops.description: Number of lookups that must be composed (chain_lookup).

steps.description: Sequential operations to simulate (state_machine, sequence_mod, arith_chain).

operand_magnitude.description: Approximate size of numbers involved (max operand).

knob.description: Name of the one difficulty field this family's ladder varies (v2 ladders).

knob_value.description: Value of that field for this item.

precedence_matters.description: True if the input matches more than one rule and order decides the answer.

distractors.description: Rules that can never fire for the input.

world_knowledge.description: How much factual knowledge the input requires beyond the rules.

level.description: Ladder position. 1-5 is the original ladder; 6+ are hard settings added to find each family's failure point.

representation_dependence.description: Whether the task leans on the surface form of the input. 'none' is the target; 'spelling' items (letter counts etc.) are discouraged because they conflate tokenization with reasoning.

rationale.description: One-line derivation of the gold answer, for auditing.
